---
title: "Numerology and the Moon"
subtitle: "A step function of the calendar against a smooth motion of the sky"
description: "Day-by-day numerology planet against the Moon's sidereal longitude and nakshatra lord, 2020-2024."
---

Date numerology assigns each calendar day a number (the day of the month
reduced to one digit) and through it a planet; the label jumps at every
midnight and repeats every month. The Moon's nakshatra lord comes from the
Moon's sidereal longitude, which moves smoothly through the 27 nakshatras of
13 degrees 20 minutes each, about one a day. The study asked whether the two
labels agree more often than chance; its pre-registered answer is in the
[paper](../../studies/numerology_vs_astrology/paper/NUMEROLOGY_ASTROLOGY_TEMPORAL_DISCONTINUITY.qmd).

::: {.af-howto}
**How to read this.** Move the slider to pick a year. The upper panel is the
Moon's sidereal longitude at noon UTC each day, rising smoothly and wrapping
at 360 degrees once a sidereal month; the faint lines are nakshatra
boundaries. The lower panel shows, for each day, the planet that date
numerology assigns (top strip) and the lord of the Moon's nakshatra (bottom
strip), coloured by planet; a dark tick marks a day on which they agree. The
calendar strip repeats its pattern every month while the Moon's drifts
against it, so agreements fall where the two cycles happen to line up. Switch
to step lines to see the same two labels as series.
:::


::: {.af-filters}

```{ojs}
viewof year = Inputs.range([2020, 2024], { label: "Year", step: 1, value: 2024 })
```

```{ojs}
viewof chart = Inputs.radio(["Planet strips", "Step lines"], { label: "Chart", value: "Planet strips" })
```

:::

```{ojs}
dayRows = {
  const c = num.columns;
  return c.date.map((t, i) => ({
    date: new Date(t + "T12:00:00Z"), day0: new Date(t + "T00:00:00Z"), year: +t.slice(0, 4),
    number: c.number[i], numPlanet: c.num_planet[i], nakLord: c.nak_lord[i],
    moon: c.moon[i], nakshatra: c.nakshatra[i]
  })).filter((d) => d.year === year);
}
planetOrder = PLANETS.map((d) => d.id)
agree = dayRows.filter((d) => d.numPlanet === d.nakLord)
expected = {
  const n = dayRows.length;
  const pa = d3.rollup(dayRows, (v) => v.length / n, (d) => d.numPlanet);
  const pb = d3.rollup(dayRows, (v) => v.length / n, (d) => d.nakLord);
  return d3.sum(planetOrder, (p) => (pa.get(p) || 0) * (pb.get(p) || 0));
}
```

```{ojs}
numChart = {
  const w = Math.max(340, Math.min(width, 1200));
  const margins = { marginLeft: 120, marginRight: 24 };
  const x = { type: "utc", domain: [new Date(Date.UTC(year, 0, 1)), new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, 0, 1))], label: null };
  const moonPlot = Plot.plot({
    ...margins, width: w, height: 240, marginTop: 24, style: plotStyle, x,
    y: { domain: [0, 360], ticks: d3.range(0, 361, 60), label: "Moon, sidereal longitude (deg)" },
    color: { type: "identity" },
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY(d3.range(0, 360, 360 / 27), { stroke: palette.grid }),
      Plot.line(unwrapRows(dayRows, "moon"), { x: "date", y: "moon", stroke: palette.planet("MOON"), strokeWidth: 2 }),
      Plot.tip(dayRows, Plot.pointerX({ x: "date", y: "moon",
        title: (d) => `${d.day0.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}\nMoon ${d.moon.toFixed(1)} deg, ${d.nakshatra}\nnakshatra lord ${d.nakLord}; numerology ${d.number} (${d.numPlanet})` }))
    ]
  });
  const ROWS = ["Numerology planet", "Moon's nakshatra lord"];
  const strips = dayRows.flatMap((d) => [
    { ...d, row: ROWS[0], planet: d.numPlanet }, { ...d, row: ROWS[1], planet: d.nakLord }
  ]);
  const lower = chart === "Planet strips"
    ? Plot.plot({
        ...margins, width: w, height: 150, style: plotStyle, x,
        y: { domain: [...ROWS, "Agree"], label: null },
        color: { type: "identity" },
        marks: [
          Plot.barX(strips, { x1: "day0", x2: (d) => d3.utcDay.offset(d.day0, 1), y: "row", fill: (d) => palette.planet(d.planet),
            title: (d) => `${d.day0.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}: ${d.row} ${d.planet}`, tip: true }),
          Plot.tickX(agree, { x: "date", y: () => "Agree", stroke: palette.ink, strokeWidth: 2,
            title: (d) => `${d.day0.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}: both ${d.nakLord}` })
        ]
      })
    : Plot.plot({
        ...margins, width: w, height: 300, style: plotStyle, x,
        y: { domain: planetOrder, label: null, tickFormat: (p) => palette.planetInfo(p).name, grid: true },
        color: { type: "identity" },
        marks: [
          Plot.line(dayRows, { x: "day0", y: "numPlanet", curve: "step-after", stroke: palette.series[1], strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
          Plot.line(dayRows, { x: "day0", y: "nakLord", curve: "step-after", stroke: palette.series[0], strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "4 2" }),
          Plot.tip(dayRows, Plot.pointerX({ x: "day0", y: "nakLord",
            title: (d) => `${d.day0.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}: numerology ${d.numPlanet}, nakshatra lord ${d.nakLord}` }))
        ]
      });
  return htl.html`<div class="af-chart" id="numerology-chart">${moonPlot}${lower}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
chart === "Planet strips"
  ? planetLegend(planetOrder)
  : swatchLegend([
      { color: palette.series[1], label: "Numerology planet (calendar)" },
      { color: palette.series[0], label: "Moon's nakshatra lord (sky)", dashed: true }
    ])
```

```{ojs}
htl.html`<p class="af-caption">${year}: the two labels agree on ${agree.length} of
  ${dayRows.length} days (${(100 * agree.length / dayRows.length).toFixed(1)}%); the agreement
  expected by chance from how often each label occurs that year is
  ${(100 * expected).toFixed(1)}%. Over 2020-2024 the study's Cohen's kappa is
  ${num.kappa.kappa.toFixed(3)} (90% interval ${num.kappa.ci90_tost[0].toFixed(3)} to
  ${num.kappa.ci90_tost[1].toFixed(3)}), against a pre-registered equivalence margin of
  plus or minus ${num.kappa.margin_kappa}.</p>`
```
